subject: BridgePoint: Follow-up on Cross-Border Transfer / DPF questionnaire
messages:
From: Alex Kramer <alex.kramer@bridgepointhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@bridgepointhealth.com
Date: 2028-07-22T15:12:00Z
Subject: Cross-border transfer questionnaire — BridgePoint DPF template

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the call earlier. As discussed, please find attached our standardized Data Protection Framework (DPF) questionnaire. We need a completed template and supporting evidence focused specifically on cross-border data transfers from the EU to the US and any other third countries.

Key items we need from Redwood:
- Confirm legal mechanism(s) relied on for EU->US transfers (SCCs, DPF adequacy, or other).
- Latest subprocessor list and whether any subprocessors process personal data outside the EU.
- Technical controls and evidence for encryption in transit and at rest (TLS versions, KMS/HSM details).
- Operational evidence for logging/retention, access controls, and audit trails (sample log excerpt acceptable).
- Any supplementary safeguards (pseudonymization, tokenization, minimal data exports).
- Confirmation of retention periods and erasure workflow for customer-controlled data.

We need the completed template and attachments within 72 hours if possible — we're on a procurement timeline and need to close the security review by next week. If there are items you cannot disclose, mark them and provide an expected timeline for delivery.

Attachment: BridgePoint_DPF_Template.xlsx (Excel questionnaire)

Best,
Alex Kramer
Head of Security & Privacy, BridgePoint Health
alex.kramer@bridgepointhealth.com
+44 20 7946 0156

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-07-22T15:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Cross-border transfer questionnaire — BridgePoint DPF template

Thanks Alex (forwarded to internal team).

Monica / Rishi — assigning tasks below so we can turn this around within the 72h ask.

- Monica: lead on contractual/legal responses (SCCs, DPA annex, lawful basis). Please draft the legal text for the DPA annex and indicate whether we rely on EU SCCs + UK Addendum for transfers. Also confirm whether we can include a redacted subprocessor list or need an NDA to share full details.
- Rishi: assemble technical evidence (TLS, KMS, HSM, key rotation, encryption-at-rest details), extract a small anonymized log sample showing access and deletion events, and prepare notes on our prefix/KV caching policy that affects cross-border caching.
- I'll own the final compilation and cover note to BridgePoint. I'll also confirm timeline and follow up on any items they mark as "cannot disclose."

Target internal deliverable in 6 hours (first-pass draft). Final package to BridgePoint in ~3-4 hours after internal review. If either of you foresee blocker questions (procurement/legal asks that need exec signoff), flag them and I'll escalate.

Thanks — Naomi

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-22T16:48:00Z
Subject: Draft responses & evidence index for BridgePoint DPF

Hi team,

Attached is a draft evidence bundle and a completed version of the BridgePoint template for review. Highlights / notes: 

1) Legal mechanism: We rely on the EU Commission standard contractual clauses (SCCs) as implemented in our DPA (signed with customers), along with the UK Addendum where relevant. We also offer customers the option to self-host via Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) where transfers are not acceptable.

2) Subprocessors: We can provide a redacted list of subprocessors publicly; full names and locations require an NDA / partner portal access. The redacted list shows categories and regions; a full CSV is included in the evidence pack under "subprocessors.csv" (see attached zip).

3) Supplementary safeguards: We apply application-level pseudonymization for optional customer data fields, strict data minimization, and configurable tokenization for PII. Note: We do not perform systematic aggregation for export; we minimize exported fields by default.

4) Retention & erasure: Customer-configurable retention with documented deletion job; timeline for irreversible deletion depends on storage tier (up to 30 days for backups). Workflow described in attachment.

Attachments included in the zip: redwood-evidence-pack.zip containing:
- SCCs-and-Addendum-summary.pdf
- subprocessors.csv (redacted)
- logs_sample_anonymized.txt (access + deletion events)
- kms-hsm-overview.pdf

I've left a few answer placeholders where we need Rishi to confirm protocol versions and a sample log excerpt sanitized for BridgePoint.

On disclosure: legal is okay to share the SCC summary and redacted subprocessor list now; full subprocessors CSV we prefer to share following an executed DPA or via our partners portal.

- Monica
Monica Patel
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Kramer <alex.kramer@bridgepointhealth.com>
Cc: legal@bridgepointhealth.com, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-22T18:04:00Z
Subject: RE: Cross-border transfer questionnaire — BridgePoint DPF template

Alex — thanks for the template and timeline. Attached is our completed DPF template plus an evidence bundle (redacted where required). Summary of key responses below: 

- Transfer mechanism: EU Commission SCCs are the primary legal mechanism for EU->US transfers; we apply the SCCs in the DPA with customers. For UK customers we attach the UK Addendum. Customers may also choose Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) to avoid transfers. (See SCCs-and-Addendum-summary.pdf)

- Subprocessors: A redacted subprocessor list is included. Full subprocessor CSV is available under NDA or via our partner portal. (See subprocessors.csv in the evidence zip.)

- Encryption & keys: All in-transit connections use TLS 1.2+; we recommend TLS 1.3 where clients support it. Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256 with customer-key options via KMS/HSM; details in kms-hsm-overview.pdf.

- Logging & retention: Sample anonymized log excerpt showing access and deletion events attached (logs_sample_anonymized.txt). Deletion workflow documented; backups retained up to 30 days with secure overwrites thereafter.

- Additional safeguards: Application-level pseudonymization and minimal export policies applied by default. We can discuss further technical pseudonymization steps for high-risk fields.

Attachments: redwood-evidence-pack.zip, SCCs-and-Addendum-summary.pdf

If you need additional extracts (e.g., full subprocessors CSV, SOC2 artifacts, or raw configuration snippets) please let us know what the reviewers need and we can either provide under NDA or route via your vendor portal.

HubSpot deal: BP-2028-014 (link: https://hubspot.company.com/deals/BP-2028-014) — I'm tagging this to legal for a quick check on the redaction level.

Best regards,
Naomi Feldman

Redwood Inference
